item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The figure below shows a spinner with 24 sectors. When someone spins the arrow, it is equally likely to stop on any sector.

[Image: Spinner with 24 sectors]

1/8 of the sectors are blue, 1/24 are purple, 1/2 are orange, and 1/3 are red. If a person spins the arrow, on which color sector is the spinner LEAST likely to stop?

options.label: A
options.text: blue

options.label: B
options.text: purple

options.label: C
options.text: orange

options.label: D
options.text: red

item.figure_description: A circular spinner divided equally into 24 sectors by radial line segments from a central pivot point. An arrow is mounted at the center, pointing toward the sector at approximately the 1 o'clock position. The sectors are plain white and unlabeled.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Spinner]

Roland’s spinner has three sectors of different colors, orange, purple, and green. Roland spins the pointer 1000 times. The chart below shows how many times the pointer stops on each section.

| Color | Times Stopped |
| :--- | :---: |
| Orange | 510 |
| Purple | 243 |
| Green | 247 |

Draw lines on the spinner above to make the three sectors the approximate size you would expect them to be. Label them orange, purple, and green.

descriptors: Orange sector approximately half the circle, green and purple each approximately one-quarter, all correctly labeled
Only one labeled sector the correct size
Three sectors drawn but none the correct size
Three sectors of correct size drawn but no labels
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: A circular spinner with a central circular hub and an arrow pointer angled upward and to the right. Around the circumference of the circle is an outer rim with 8 equally spaced tick marks, dividing the circle into 8 equal arcs of 45° each (at 12 o'clock, 1:30, 3 o'clock, 4:30, 6 o'clock, 7:30, 9 o'clock, and 10:30). The interior of the circle is blank.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A spinner, which is divided and labeled with purple, orange, green, blue, and red. The purple section takes up half of the spinner. The orange section takes up one fourth of the spinner. The green, blue, and red sections each take up one twelfth of the spinner.]

The spinner is for Steve's new game. Out of 600 spins, approximately how many times should he expect the arrow to land on the red sector?
reference_items.figure_description: A circular spinner with a central pivot dot and an arrow pointing toward the upper right. The circle is divided into five sectors by radius lines. A vertical diameter splits the circle: the entire right half is a single semicircle labeled 'Purple'. The top-left quadrant is labeled 'Orange'. The bottom-left quadrant is divided into three equal slices, labeled from top to bottom as 'Green', 'Blue', and 'Red'.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Color of Caps

[Image: A pie chart indicating 30% white caps, 25% green caps, 15% black caps, 10% blue caps, and 20% red caps.]

The pie chart shows the percentage of caps for sale at a sporting goods store. If there are 200 caps, what is the total number of caps that are either white or green?
reference_items.figure_description: A pie chart titled "Color of Caps" divided into five sectors: White (labeled "White 30%") occupying the top-left sector; Green (labeled "Green 25%") occupying the top-right quadrant; Red (labeled "Red 20%") occupying the bottom-right sector; Blue (labeled "Blue 10%") occupying a narrow sector at the bottom; and Black (labeled "Black 15%") occupying the sector between Blue and White on the lower left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Sophie has a bag in which there are 16 marbles: 8 are red and 8 are black marbles. She draws 2 marbles from the bag and does not put them back. Both marbles are black. She then draws a third marble out of the bag. What can you say about the likely color of this third marble?

options.label: A
options.text: It is more likely to be red than black.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely to be black than red.

options.label: C
options.text: It is equally likely to be red or black.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot tell if red or black is more likely.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A machine has 100 candies and dispenses a candy when a lever is turned. The machine has the same number of blue, pink, yellow, and green candies all mixed together. Megan turned the lever and obtained a pink candy. Peter turned the lever next.

How likely is it that Peter will get a pink candy?

options.label: A
options.text: It is certain that his candy will be pink.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely than it was for Megan.

options.label: C
options.text: It is exactly as likely as it was for Megan.

options.label: D
options.text: It is less likely than it was for Megan.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
If a fair coin is tossed, the probability that it will land heads up is 1/2. In four successive tosses, a fair coin lands heads up each time.
What is likely to happen when the coin is tossed a fifth time?

options.label: A
options.text: It is more likely to land tails up than heads up.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely to land heads up than tails up.

options.label: C
options.text: It is equally likely to land heads up or tails up.

options.label: D
options.text: More information is needed to answer the question.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
